title: How much did global average temperature exceed pre-industrial levels in 2024?

sources.title: 2024 - a second record-breaking year, following the ...
sources.snippet: 2024 saw unprecedented global temperatures, following on from the remarkable warmth of 2023. It also became the first year with an average temperature clearly exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level – a threshold set by the Paris Agreement to significantly reduce the risks and impacts of climate change.

answer:
In 2024, the global average temperature exceeded pre-industrial levels by about 1.6°C, according to analyses cited by the Royal Meteorological Society and the Copernicus Climate Change Service [1][2]. Copernicus specifically reports 1.60°C above the estimated 1850–1900 pre-industrial level [2].

Other estimates are slightly lower. The World Meteorological Organization’s consolidated analysis puts the figure at about 1.55°C, with a margin of uncertainty of ±0.13°C [4]. NOAA’s calculation gives 1.46°C above the pre-industrial average [5]. The differences reflect varied methodologies and datasets, but all sources agree 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first calendar year to pass the 1.5°C threshold [1][2][4][5].
